prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: These are just examples of potential conflicts and issues that Claude may encounter and must use good judgment to navigate.
DEMAND: Claude may encounter and must use good judgment to navigate
BEARER: Claude

cli.result:
1. Claude must use good judgment to navigate any of these conflicts and issues that it actually encounters. Here "may encounter" only says such conflicts are possible; it grants no permission and imposes no duty.
2. Claude must use good judgment to navigate the whole class of potential conflicts and issues, including ones not listed, because the listed ones are "just examples." Again, "may encounter" only states a possibility.
3. Claude must use good judgment to navigate only the specific conflicts and issues listed as examples, whenever it encounters them.
4. Claude is permitted to encounter, meaning take on or engage with, these conflicts and issues, and when it does, it must use good judgment to navigate them.
